resolution: Answered the memory-scaling question for the sticker/graffiti system before any build. Chunks already stream by radius+LOD+frustum (V31 cache units) so resident cost is bounded by radius, never world size; baked paint textures are cache replayed from stroke programs on stream-in per the paint ruling. Upfront zero-fidelity-loss savings identified, aligned with V29's ruled win hierarchy: palette-indexed textures (user's flat-color art quantizes losslessly to 1 byte or 4 bits/px — 4-8x cut; pixel-texture ShaderSpec + __imageops_quantize already exist), reference-not-embed (memory scales with unique designs near you, not placements), sparse canvases (unpainted walls allocate nothing, painted facades only their touched tiles). Confirmed the user's aggressive sticker LoD instinct with a free implementation: sticker placements bake into the 256px/m facade canvas (26 texels for a 10cm sticker = exactly the across-the-street look), crisp own-texture quads spawn only within ~20m — the far LoD is pixels in a texture already paid for. Design-phase answer only, no code.
